subject: Clarify private offer: commit bands, metering model, and reseller uplift mechanics
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@helios-analytics.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Chung <oliver.chung@helios-analytics.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Clarifying private offer mechanics and partner margin expectations

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Helios is excited about Redwood for inference cost control and private deployment options. Procurement and finance had a few detailed questions before we move to a formal PO: 

1) Commit bands: your SDR mentioned tiered discounts at 100k / 300k / 600k annualized spend. Can you confirm what the effective list-price discounts are at each band and whether those bands are contractually enforceable for 12 months?

2) Metering model: we need clarity on seat-based vs metered tokens. Our primary use case is variable — heavy batch runs some months and low others. Do you offer a hybrid (base seats + overage metering)? How do overage rates get applied in private offers vs marketplace SKUs?

3) Channel uplift/reseller margin: Helios prefers to route via our systems integrator (Brightline) and expects a 12% reseller uplift on net ARR. How does Redwood recommend structuring the private offer so Brightline receives margin without impacting Helios list discount?

4) Billing flow: can you support a reseller invoice path (Brightline invoices Helios) and still allow us to redeem marketplace committed discounts? We need this for compliance.

Attached: initial contract template we use for marketplace POs (Helios_PO_Draft_v0.9.pdf). Would appreciate a short note on the three points above.

Thanks,
Nora
Procurement Manager
Helios Analytics
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: Oliver Chung <oliver.chung@helios-analytics.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarifying private offer mechanics and partner margin expectations

Hi Nora — great questions, thanks for the clear ask. I took this to the deal team and sketched three pragmatic paths below. I've attached an SKU mapping spreadsheet that maps marketplace SKUs to the PO line items (Helios_SKU_mapping_v1.xlsx). Quick summary first, then details.

Summary (pick one):
- Option A — Metered-only private offer: commit = annual token spend, tiered discounts applied to committed token spend, monthly metering. Best for highly variable usage; overages billed monthly at the banded overage rate.
- Option B — Seat + Overage (hybrid): reserved baseline seats for predictable throughput + metered overage. Commit covers seat subscriptions; overage discounts kick in at monthly thresholds.
- Option C — ARR-style list-price with partner uplift: maintain marketplace list price in the PO for compliance, apply a Redwood-managed reseller uplift to Brightline as a one-time partner credit (off-invoice or rebate).

Details and how they map to your asks:
1) Commit bands: the private-offer engine supports locked-in banded discounts for 12 months. Typical bands we set are 0-100k (baseline), 100k-300k (5% off list), 300k-600k (12% off list), >600k (18% off). These are configurable in the offer terms and reflected on the marketplace contract metadata so they persist for the contracted term. If you need tighter floors (e.g., minimum committed spend), we can encode that in the PO.

2) Metering model: Option A uses token-metering exclusively. Option B is what most enterprise customers choose when they have variable batch loads but need predictable baseline throughput. Hybrid mechanics we recommend:
- Define base seats (N GPUs / reserved concurrency) priced as a subscription line item.
- Meter overage per-token monthly with a blended overage rate that steps down at negotiated volumes.
For private offers, overage billing is handled through Redwood's billing connector to the marketplace; the marketplace will show the same SKU family, and private-offer metadata includes the overage price table.

3) Channel uplift / reseller margin: to avoid double-discounting we suggest one of two practical flows:
- Flow 1 (off-invoice partner credit): Helios pays Brightline at the PO price (marketplace list less private offer discount). Redwood issues Brightline a partner credit after ingestion of usage (quarterly reconciliation). Credits are netted at Redwood-Brightline settlement. This keeps the Helios invoice clean and preserves marketplace discounting.
- Flow 2 (pass-through reseller invoice): Brightline invoices Helios directly at the agreed net price; Brightline pays Redwood at the private-offer list price. The marketplace requires the private-offer metadata reflect the pass-through arrangement. This can complicate redemption of committed discounts — we can track in the private-offer metadata and reconcile usage-based true-ups on our side.
Recommended default: Flow 1 for simplicity and to ensure committed discount redemption. If Helios requires Brightline on invoice for audit, Flow 2 is possible but will need a short ops playbook.

4) Billing flow: we support both flows above. For reseller invoicing we will need Brightline's tax & vendor info to be added to the private-offer. For Flow 1 (partner credit) you do not need a reseller invoice path; reconciliation happens via partner settlement.

Next steps (proposed):
- Please confirm which option you prefer (A/B/C) and whether Brightline requires invoice routing.
- If Flow 2 is required, please share Brightline's vendor setup contact and tax ID so we can provision the pass-through metadata.

I'll loop in Ben (channel ops) and Laura (revenue ops) below to confirm settlement cadence and any finance constraints. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with Helios + Brightline to finalize.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarifying private offer mechanics and partner margin expectations

Sofia, quick internal note — copying the mail thread quote below.

On Sun, 12 Jul 2026 at 09:30, sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com> wrote:
> Summary (pick one):
> - Option A — Metered-only private offer: commit = annual token spend, tiered discounts applied to committed token spend, monthly metering. Best for highly variable usage; overages billed monthly at the banded overage rate.
> - Option B — Seat + Overage (hybrid): reserved baseline seats for predictable throughput + metered overage.
>
Action items for finance/ops before we send a final note to Helios: 
1) If we recommend Flow 1 (off-invoice partner credit), we need to confirm our partner credit ledger workflow and quarter cadence (QTR) settlement timelines. Laura — can you confirm: a) do credits net against Brightline outstanding invoices or do we do a quarterly ACH credit? Also any tax reporting implications?
2) SKU mapping: the Helios_SKU_mapping_v1.xlsx looks fine but we need to ensure our marketplace SKU ids (aws:sku:...) match the PO lines. Irene — can you validate the SKU ids and whether any SKU needs to be split for seat vs token usage?
3) Discount stack: make sure private-offer discount doesn't get applied twice if Brightline triggers a reseller discount on top. We should code a single discount source in the offer metadata (Redwood-managed) and credit Brightline separately.

I'll draft the short ops paragraph Sofia can include in the customer-facing note explaining settlement timing (Net30 credits, quarterly true-up).

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Channel Operations Manager
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@helios-analytics.com>, Oliver Chung <oliver.chung@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarifying private offer mechanics and partner margin expectations — next steps

Hi Nora / Oliver — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on your environment and audit needs we recommend Option B (Seat + Overage hybrid) with Flow 1 (off-invoice partner credit) as the cleanest path for Helios to preserve marketplace committed discounts while giving Brightline an effective 12% uplift.

Key points agreed (summary for PO):
- Structure: annual baseline seats (SKU lines 1001-1004 in the attached mapping) + metered overage by token. Baseline seats billed monthly per marketplace subscription lines.
- Commit bands and effective discounts: 0-100k (0%), 100k-300k (5%), 300k-600k (12%), >600k (18%) applied to committed token spend. Bands locked for 12 months in the private offer metadata.
- Partner uplift: Brightline will receive a 12% partner credit calculated on net ARR and settled quarterly by Redwood (off-invoice). Helios invoice remains at the private-offer net price; Brightline receives credits from Redwood.
- Reconciliation: quarterly true-up based on actual usage vs committed spend; overage rates apply monthly and will be included in the quarterly settlement.
- Ops items required from Helios: confirm Brightline vendor name for settlement (if different), or confirm you are OK with the off-invoice credit flow.

I've attached a draft PO (Helios_PO_Draft_v0.9.pdf) with the SKU mapping embedded. If this looks correct, Nora, would you: 1) confirm Brightline's vendor name for our partner ledger (if applicable), and 2) confirm you want quarterly or monthly partner credit settlement?

Proposed next step: 30-min call Monday 19 Jul 2026 with Helios procurement + Brightline (if required) + Redwood channel ops. If you prefer changes to the banding or uplift %, let us know and we can run a quick financial model to show P&L impact.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Helios_SKU_mapping_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), Helios_PO_Draft_v0.9.pdf (PDF)
